items.q: A business sells 7,500 units at £12 each. Variable cost is £10 per unit and fixed costs are £21,000. What is its profit?
items.why: Total contribution = (£12 – £10) × 7,500 = £15,000. Profit = total contribution – fixed costs = £15,000 – £21,000 = –£6,000.
items.label: New question

items.q: Use the break-even chart. What is the break-even output?
items.why: Break-even is where the total revenue and total costs lines cross, at 300 units. You can check: fixed costs £1,800 ÷ contribution per unit of £6 = 300 units.
items.label: New question

items.q: AJS plc's proposed investment. Net cash flows (£000): Year 0 (500), Year 1 (50), Year 2 250, Year 3 600. Discount factors: 1.00, 0.91, 0.83, 0.75. Calculate the net present value.
items.why: Present values: Year 1 –50 × 0.91 = –45.5; Year 2 250 × 0.83 = 207.5; Year 3 600 × 0.75 = 450. Total = 612. NPV = 612 – 500 = 112, so £112,000. Year 1 is negative, so it is taken off.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2023 Q01.1

items.q: Capital employed £30m, Current assets £4m, Current liabilities £3m, Non-current liabilities £12m. Current ratio?
items.why: Current ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities = 4/3 = 1.33:1. Express as a ratio, not a percentage or absolute figure. The current ratio is always expressed as X:1.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Revenue £42m, cost of sales £20m, operating expenses £12m, net finance costs £3m, taxation £2m. What is the gross profit?
items.why: Gross profit = revenue – cost of sales = £42m – £20m = £22m.
items.label: New question

items.q: A project costs £400,000 and lasts 4 years. Net cash flows are Year 1: £130,000; Year 2: £60,000; Year 3: £180,000; Year 4: £130,000. What is the average rate of return (ARR)?
items.why: Total net cash flow = £500,000. Total profit = £500,000 – £400,000 = £100,000. Average annual profit = £100,000 ÷ 4 = £25,000. ARR = £25,000 ÷ £400,000 × 100 = 6.2%. Taking off the cost of the investment is the step most often missed.
items.label: New question

items.q: A retailer has revenue of £1,080,000, cost of sales of £720,000 and average inventory of £75,000. What is its inventory turnover?
items.why: Inventory turnover = cost of sales ÷ average inventory = £720,000 ÷ £75,000 = 9.6 times a year.
items.label: New question

items.q: AJS plc, 2022: non-current liabilities £4m, operating profit £3m, gearing 22%. Calculate its return on capital employed.
items.why: Gearing = non-current liabilities ÷ capital employed, so capital employed = £4m ÷ 0.22 = £18.18m. ROCE = £3m ÷ £18.18m × 100 = 16.5%.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2023 Q01.2

items.q: Zero inventory. Buffer level = 80 units. Uses 35 units/day. Lead time = 5 days. Reorder level = ?
items.why: Reorder level = (daily usage x lead time) + buffer stock = (35 x 5) + 80 = 175 + 80 = 255 units. Students often forget to add the buffer stock, getting 175. The reorder level must include the buffer to ensure stock never falls below the safety level.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A business has revenue of £740,000 and receivables of £45,000. What are its receivables days?
items.why: Receivables days = receivables ÷ revenue × 365 = £45,000 ÷ £740,000 × 365 = 22.2, about 22 days.
items.label: New question
